title: Universality of Turing equivalence
formal: Is unrestricted Turing equivalence universal among countable Borel equivalence relations? Precisely, is the following proposition true: for every standard Borel space \(X\) and every Borel equivalence relation \(E\subseteq X\times X\) whose equivalence classes are at most countable, there exists a Borel map \(f:X\to2^{\mathbb N}\) such that \[\forall x,y\in X,\qquad x\,E\,y\ \Longleftrightarrow\ f(x)\equiv_T f(y)?\] The map may depend on \(X\) and \(E\); both implications must hold on every pair.
definitions:
Write \(\mathbb N=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}\). Cantor space \(2^{\mathbb N}=\{0,1\}^{\mathbb N}\) contains all infinite binary sequences, with the product topology of the discrete two-point space; its basic open cylinders specify a finite initial segment. Fix an effective enumeration \((\Phi_e)_{e\in\mathbb N}\) of ordinary oracle Turing programs. For \(a,b\in2^{\mathbb N}\), define \(a\le_T b\) by \(\exists e\,\forall n\in\mathbb N\,[\Phi_e^b(n)\text{ halts with output }a(n)]\). One program must work for every coordinate; its index may depend on the ordered pair \((a,b)\). It may query individual bits of \(b\), with no time or space bound and no additional oracle. Define \(a\equiv_T b\) by \(a\le_T b\) and \(b\le_T a\). Finite strings and machine descriptions are encoded by any fixed effective encoding, which does not change this reducibility.

A Polish topology is a topology induced by a complete separable metric. A standard Borel space is a set equipped with the Borel sigma-algebra of some Polish topology; the Borel sigma-algebra is the smallest family containing the open sets and closed under complements and countable unions. Equip \(X\times X\) with the product Borel structure. The relation \(E\) is a Borel subset of this product and is reflexive, symmetric and transitive. Each class \([x]_E=\{y\in X:x\,E\,y\}\) must be finite or countably infinite; \(X\) itself may be uncountable. A map is Borel if the inverse image of every Borel set is Borel. For a map to Cantor space it suffices to check inverse images of its basic cylinders. The notation \(E\le_B F\) means that a Borel map preserves both equivalence and inequivalence between \(E\) and \(F\) on all pairs.

An equivalent single-relation formulation uses the following fixed \(E_{\infty}\). Let \(F_2\) be the free group on two generators \(a,b\): its elements are finite reduced words in \(a,a^{-1},b,b^{-1}\), with no adjacent inverse letters; multiplication concatenates words and cancels adjacent inverse pairs, the empty word is the identity, and inversion reverses the word and inverts each letter. Give \(2^{F_2}\), the set of all functions \(F_2\to\{0,1\}\), the product topology, whose basic cylinders prescribe values at finitely many group elements. Define \[x\,E_{\infty}\,y\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists g\in F_2\,\forall h\in F_2,\ y(h)=x(g^{-1}h).\] This particular countable Borel equivalence relation is known to be universal, so the main target is equivalent to \(E_{\infty}\le_B\equiv_T\).

The question concerns ordinary classical mathematics, with no additional determinacy or unproved conjectural assumption. The requested reduction need not be computable, continuous or injective on individual points; its induced map on equivalence classes must be injective. There is no requirement for an algorithmic transformation from a code for \(E\) to a code for \(f\), no prescribed dependence of output program indices on input equivalence witnesses, and no exception on a null or meager set. Neither a probability measure nor a resource bound is part of the target.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the displayed universality proposition or its negation, including all necessary definitions and background results. A positive answer establishes the existence of a Borel reduction for every stated \((X,E)\); an equivalent positive theorem gives a Borel reduction of the explicitly defined \(E_{\infty}\), together with the theorem establishing its universality. No effective construction of all reductions is required. A negative answer establishes one countable Borel equivalence relation \(E\) for which every Borel map \(f:X\to2^{\mathbb N}\) fails the biconditional for at least one pair \(x,y\); equivalently, prove this failure for every Borel map on the stated \(E_{\infty}\) domain. The counterexample pair may depend on \(f\). A theorem conditional on Martin’s conjecture, failure only of uniform or computable reductions, or universality of a different degree relation does not settle the target. This is an exact yes/no question, with no numerical tolerance.
why: A central bridge between computability and descriptive set theory, asking whether equality of computational power can encode every countable Borel classification problem.

importance.reason: A classical universality question with consequences for Martin’s conjecture and for the distinction between definable and uniform computational encodings.

progress.text: Kechris’s universality question is recorded in the historical sources surveyed by Caicedo–Löwe.
Marks–Slaman–Steel publish the universality proof for arithmetic equivalence and explain the conflict between Turing universality and Martin’s conjecture.
Marks proves universality of polynomial-time Turing equivalence; online publication is 2016 and the journal issue is 2018.

Kechris’s book preprint retains Turing universality as Problem 12.5.

status_note: Checked through 16 September 2026. No unconditional proof or refutation of ordinary Borel universality of unrestricted Turing equivalence was found in the bounded primary-source review. Arithmetic and polynomial-time universality, nonuniversality for specified uniform generators, the conditional Martin-conjecture obstruction and the conditional February 2026 Day–Marks consequences concern distinct statements. The erroneous equivalence characterization in MSS Theorem 1.8 is excluded following the author erratum.

context_blocks.text: Two infinite binary sequences have the same Turing degree when each can compute the other. This partitions all possible oracles by their computational power. The universality question asks how complicated that partition is as a classification problem: can every countable Borel pattern of equivalence be represented exactly by equality of Turing degrees? The objects being classified are infinite sequences, not finite machine descriptions.

There are countably many oracle programs. Consequently, for a fixed oracle b, only countably many sequences can be computed from b, and its Turing-equivalence class is countable. The relation is Borel because a claim that an oracle program computes a given sequence can be written using countably many conditions about finite computations. Thus Turing equivalence itself belongs to the class of relations compared on this card.

A Borel reduction is a structured assignment of invariants. If f reduces E to Turing equivalence, the Turing degree of \(f(x)\) is a complete invariant for the E-class of x: equivalent objects receive the same degree, and inequivalent objects receive different degrees. Distinct representatives of one E-class may receive different binary sequences, provided those sequences have the same degree. Injectivity on equivalence classes is essential; injectivity on individual points is not.

The explicitly defined shift relation \(E_{\infty}\) is a universal countable Borel equivalence relation: every such relation reduces to it. This theorem of Dougherty, Jackson and Kechris makes the single question \(E_{\infty}\le_B\equiv_T\) equivalent to the full target. The space here includes all binary labelings of the free group, including labelings with nontrivial stabilizers.

The inherited Caicedo–Löwe survey records the question as Question 6 in its discussion of Martin’s conjecture. It traces the universality problem to Kechris and distinguishes it from nearby statements about arithmetic equivalence and uniform coding. The source is a 2019 preprint; the later published chapter updates the year in its title. The card retains the exact inherited version and locator.

There are strong positive results for neighboring relations. Slaman and Steel proved that arithmetic equivalence is universal; Marks, Slaman and Steel provide a published proof and discussion. Arithmetic equivalence allows each sequence to be computed from some finite Turing jump of the other, with the finite jump levels depending on the pair. That extra allowance changes which sequences become equivalent.

In the other direction, Marks proved universality of polynomial-time Turing equivalence, as well as polynomial-time many-one equivalence. These compare arbitrary languages over finite strings by resource-bounded oracle reductions. The theorem concerns the entire space of languages, not only decidable languages or languages inside a familiar complexity class. It establishes universality for a finer relation than unrestricted Turing equivalence.

Universality does not automatically pass from a finer relation to a coarser one. Two encoded outputs that are inequivalent under polynomial-time reductions may nevertheless be equivalent under unrestricted oracle computation. That collapses distinct source classes and violates the reverse implication required of a Borel reduction.

A related negative theorem concerns uniform universality with respect to specified generating maps. When Turing equivalence is generated by its usual oracle-program reductions, it is not uniformly universal. Uniformity would require the two output computation indices to depend only on the indices witnessing the input equivalence, independently of the input objects. This extra requirement is absent from the target.

The choice of generators matters for uniform universality. Marks shows that a universal countable Borel relation can always be given some generating family for which it is uniformly universal. Consequently, the negative result for the standard Turing-program generators does not itself rule out an arbitrary Borel reduction.

The Borel form of Martin’s conjecture implies nonuniversality of Turing equivalence: it even rules out a Borel reduction of two disjoint copies of Turing equivalence into one copy. This is a conditional consequence, not an unconditional answer.

Day and Marks’ February 2026 revision studies whether Turing equivalence is an increasing union of Borel equivalence relations whose stages omit certain uniformly computable infinite sequences. A positive answer would imply nonuniform invariant functions and universality of ordinary many-one equivalence. These are conditional consequences of a different open decomposition question. The article is published in Transactions of the American Mathematical Society, Series B 13 (2026), 379–402.

Settling the card would tell us whether mutual computability provides a universal language for countable Borel classification, or has a structural limitation absent from some nearby degree notions. Either outcome would matter beyond computability: it would constrain the ways orbit equivalence relations, invariants and definable encodings can interact. The answer criterion is a precise existence theorem for reductions, with no algorithmic-efficiency requirement hidden inside the word “Borel.”

The author erratum to the Marks–Slaman–Steel survey identifies an incorrect equivalence assertion in Theorem 1.8 concerning formulations of Martin’s conjecture. That characterization is not used as an established theorem on this card.

sentences: Turing equivalence groups all infinite binary sequences according to mutual oracle computability, without time or space restrictions.
The question asks whether every Borel equivalence relation with countable classes can be encoded by Turing degrees using a Borel map.
The encoding must preserve both equivalence and inequivalence for every input pair, but need not be computable, continuous or uniform on computation indices.
The explicitly defined binary shift of the free group on two generators gives an equivalent single universal relation whose reducibility would settle the whole question.

A complete Lean proof must establish or refute this exact universality statement; neighboring universality theorems and conditional Martin-conjecture or 2026 decomposition consequences do not suffice.
